title: 醉太平·讥贪小利者
titlePy: Zuì Tài Píng · Jī Tān Xiǎo Lì Zhě
titleEn: Drunk in Peacetime: Mocking the Petty and Greedy
author: 佚名（元曲）
intro: A comic, biting song about greedy people who will scrape profit from anywhere — mud from a swallow’s beak, gold leaf from a Buddha’s face, fat from inside a mosquito. Wild exaggeration, very funny.
analysis: 这是一首讽刺小令，用夸张得近乎荒唐的比喻，嘲笑那些贪得无厌、连一点点小便宜都不放过的人。全曲一口气列出七件“不可能的事”：从燕子嘴里抢泥（燕子筑巢用的一点泥），从针头上削铁，从佛像脸上刮金箔，在什么都没有的地方硬找出东西来；在鹌鹑的嗉子里找豌豆，在鹭鸶细细的腿上割瘦肉，在蚊子肚子里挖油——最后一句冷冷地说：“亏老先生下手！”真难为您老人家下得了手。这种把同一类比喻一个接一个排列的写法叫“排比”，越排越夸张，讽刺的力量越来越强。元曲语言通俗、泼辣，敢说敢骂，这首就是典型。今天“鹭鸶腿上劈精肉”“蚊子腹内刳脂油”仍被用来形容极端的吝啬和贪婪。
analysisEn: This is a satirical song that mocks people so greedy they won’t pass up even the tiniest gain, using comparisons so exaggerated they become absurd. In one breath it lists seven impossible feats: snatching mud from a swallow’s beak (the little bit it carries to build its nest), shaving iron off the tip of a needle, scraping the gold leaf off a Buddha statue’s face — finding something where there is nothing. Then: hunting for a pea in a quail’s crop, carving lean meat from an egret’s skinny leg, digging fat out of a mosquito’s belly. And the last line, dry and cutting: “How can you bring yourself to do it, sir!” Piling up comparisons of the same kind, each more extreme than the last, is a favourite device in Chinese writing, and here every new image sharpens the mockery. Yuan songs are known for plain, earthy, outspoken language — they are not afraid to ridicule — and this one is a perfect example. Some of its lines are still used today to describe extreme stinginess and greed.
background: The author is unknown. The song survives in Yuan-dynasty anthologies of sanqu, popular song lyrics written to fixed tunes, which often poked fun at social vices.
pronunciation: 削铁：削 xuē。觅 mì。鹌鹑 ān chún。嗉 sù。鹭鸶 lù sī。劈 pī。刳 kū（剖开挖空）。脂 zhī。
version: 采用通行版本。“亏老先生下手”有本作“亏老先生下手了”，网站不用。

lines.py: duó ní yàn kǒu, xuē tiě zhēn tóu
lines.lit: Snatch mud from a swallow’s mouth, shave iron from a needle’s tip,
lines.en: He’d snatch the mud from a swallow’s beak, shave iron off a needle’s point,

lines.py: guā jīn fó miàn xì sōu qiú
lines.lit: scrape gold from a Buddha’s face, searching carefully,
lines.en: scrape the gilt from a Buddha’s face, searching every inch —
he’ll find something where there’s nothing.

lines.py: ān chún sù lǐ xún wān dòu
lines.lit: In a quail’s crop he looks for peas,
lines.en: He’d hunt for a pea in a quail’s crop,

lines.py: lù sī tuǐ shàng pī jīng ròu
lines.lit: on an egret’s leg he chops lean meat,
lines.en: carve lean meat from an egret’s leg,

lines.py: wén zi fù nèi kū zhī yóu
lines.lit: inside a mosquito’s belly he scoops out fat —
lines.en: dig the fat out of a mosquito’s belly —

lines.py: kuī lǎo xiān shēng xià shǒu
lines.lit: It takes you, old sir, to lay hands on it!
lines.en: Only you, good sir, could bring yourself to do it!

words.note: 单用口语读 xiāo，如“削苹果”；在复合词里读 xuē，如“削铁如泥”“剥削”。
觅：寻找，现代汉语“寻觅”。今天常说“无中生有”，意思是凭空捏造，不同。
今天南方话仍说“精肉”，普通话说“瘦肉”。

words.en: to cut open and hollow out
(ironic) it takes (someone) to…; how could you
words.note: 现代口语“亏你想得出来”“亏你说得出口”，表示讽刺。

imagery.name: 燕
imagery.zh: 燕子衔泥筑巢，一口泥极少，连这都要抢，可见贪得可笑。
imagery.en: A swallow carries only a beakful of mud for its nest; robbing even that shows absurd greed.

imagery.name: 鸟
imagery.zh: 鹌鹑的嗉子、鹭鸶的细腿都几乎榨不出什么，用这些小鸟夸张地讽刺贪小利的人。
imagery.en: A quail’s crop, an egret’s stick-thin leg — there is almost nothing to take, which makes the greed laughable.
